cards.title: Borrowed Authority
cards.instruction: Project confident authority while quietly working to keep everyone cooperative. Your confidence depends on their cooperation.

cards.title: Hand It Over
cards.instruction: Persuade someone to give up control of a task, object, or decision you believe is being mishandled.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me fix that cupboard hinge. The door's lower than when you started.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm just finding the right screw.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've tried four. Give me the screwdriver while you find it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then you'll tell everyone you fixed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You can announce the repair. I'll stand behind you with the screwdriver, keeping the door attached.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me handle the seating plan. You've put the exes together.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: They're civil now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then they can be civil from separate tables.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've spent hours on it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Give me the pencil. I'll preserve the hours and move the chairs.

cards.title: Borrowed Authority

cards.title: Put It Back Quietly
cards.instruction: Return something you misplaced, used, or damaged without revealing why it needed restoring.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've put your umbrella back in the stand. You'll want it for work.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why is it wet? It hasn't rained.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I gave it a rinse. I'll dry the handle before you go.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's pondweed caught in the spokes.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then it needs another rinse. Have breakfast; I'll get it back in the stand properly this time.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your plate's back in the cupboard, ready for Sunday lunch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That one's got flowers. Ours were plain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll take that one. The potatoes will cover the flowers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'm not hiding it under potatoes. I want six matching plates.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll get five more before lunch. Keep the plain ones for spares; there's no need to count those today.

cards.title: Talk Around the Mess
cards.instruction: Keep attention on minor details so no one addresses the larger responsibility you avoided.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Mum's coming for lunch. Is this spoon clean enough for her? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The spoon's fine. You haven't cleaned the kitchen.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. She checks cutlery. Could you check the forks while I finish this?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I've told her to bring rubber gloves and help you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then we need a guest towel. Can you help me choose one without a faded stripe?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

cards.title: Spare Them the Hassle
cards.instruction: Hide a practical problem because you believe handling it alone is kinder than involving anyone else.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Sit down, love. You've been on the ward all night. I'll bring lunch. Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's there a bucket by my chair?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. Just catching a drip. Take the sofa; I've made you a tray.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll eat upstairs and go straight to bed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Stay here. I'll bring your duvet down; upstairs needs a little drying before I put your bed back.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: As your new shift leader, I'm moving lunch to twelve.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Twelve was the consultation time. Eleven is my decision.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Naturally. I'll announce that before anyone else does.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm captain of this rowing team. Everybody rows on my whistle.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We prefer counting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll whistle the numbers.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. A captain adapts. You'll still call me captain?

beats.text: Sit down, love. You've been on the ward all night. I'll bring lunch.

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Enjoy your afternoon off. Your bike will be ready for tomorrow.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Why's the repair shop asking me to collect a wheel?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: They've got your number on the ticket. I'll collect everything.

beats.text: A wheel? Is the rest at another shop?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Only until four. Stay with your book; I've planned a route that gets all of it home before you need it.

cards.title: Who Changed It?
cards.instruction: Ask innocent questions until someone admits altering the plan, schedule, arrangement, or shared space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'd like to keep this voluntary. Interesting. The picnic moved from Saturday to Friday. Whose blue pen is that? Please.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Mine, but everyone uses it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'm still in charge; we can make an adjustment. And whose handwriting adds hearts to Fridays?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: All right, I changed it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely. Now, who should tell the Saturday guests?

beats.text: The crew eats at eleven.

beats.text: We also leave early on Fridays.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Could you just count?

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: B

beats.speaker: A

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I can't open the cupboard. Was the sofa this close yesterday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: There's more room for yoga now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Did making that room involve moving the sofa?

beats.text: Yes, I moved it. I put the things you'll need somewhere easier.

beats.text: How thoughtful. Would those be the mugs in your sock drawer, or has someone else improved the kitchen too?
